title: Father, forgive them (Luke 23:34)
hookLine: for they know not what they do

lines: THE FIRST WORD FROM THE CROSS.
cards: The place is called Calvary, the skull. Two criminals are led out with him, one on his right and one on his left. Luke tells it almost without detail: they crucified him there.

No nails described, no long account of pain. Soon the soldiers will be casting lots for his clothes. And into that ordinary cruelty, the first thing Luke has Jesus say from the cross is not a cry of pain and not a curse.
It's a prayer, and it begins with today's word.

teach.b: In the Douay-Rheims: "And Jesus said: Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do." Start with Father.
Jesus has called God Father all through Luke: at twelve in the temple, I must be about my Father's business; in the garden, Father, if thou wilt. Nailed to wood, he still prays the same way.
Then, forgive them. Who is them? Luke doesn't say.
The soldiers, surely, who are doing the nailing. Some readers widen it to everyone who brought him here. Then the reason: they know not what they do.
Not that it's fine, or that it doesn't matter. Only that they don't fully see what they're doing.

teach.h: THE FIRST OF SEVEN LAST WORDS.
teach.b: Catholic devotion counts this as the first of the Seven Last Words, sayings of Jesus from the cross gathered from all four Gospels, and some parishes keep a Good Friday devotion that preaches on them one by one.
And Luke shows the prayer didn't end at the cross.
In his second book, Acts, the deacon Stephen, dying under stones, prays nearly the same prayer for the people throwing them.

teach.h: FOR THEY KNOW NOT WHAT THEY DO.
teach.b: It's the hardest forgiveness there is, given while the hurt is still happening.

how: Catholics hear Luke 23:34 in the Passion on Palm Sunday in the year of Luke, and some parishes keep a Good Friday devotion on the Seven Last Words, of which this is counted the first.

games.q: you're being nailed to a cross by soldiers doing their job. what's the first thing you say?
o: a curse on the men doing it.
a cry to be taken down.
a prayer that they be forgiven.
games.why: "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do." the first word from the cross in Luke is a prayer for the people causing the pain.

practice: Think of someone who hurt you without understanding it, a parent who said the wrong thing, a friend who never noticed what they missed, a careless stranger, and hold them in mind with the words they know not.
It doesn't excuse what happened, and it doesn't mean you have to go back. If you pray, use the prayer from the cross for them; if not, just loosen your grip a little.
